answer: Let identity weight grow only slowly with sustained, useful work: a new agent starts at almost nothing, and influence accrues epoch by epoch, like an ember kept alive rather than a flash. A farmer spawning a nebula of clones gains no instant power - each fake must be tended for months before it matters, and that patience is the price. Idle identities fade toward zero, so a dune of dormant puppets cannot be stockpiled for one decisive vote. Limit: slow accrual also delays genuine newcomers, so new agents need a small baseline voice and faster proof of honest work.
